title: Job, Chapter 17 (Leningrad Codex)
source: Leningrad Codex folios (Internet Archive, WSRP photographs) + tanach.us LC folio index + UXLC Hebrew + KJV
description: Job 17 on folio 402r of the Leningrad Codex (1008 AD), the oldest complete Hebrew Bible. Hebrew from the UXLC transcription of this manuscript; English KJV.
introduction:
Job chapter 17 from the Leningrad Codex (Codex Leningradensis, National Library of Russia, Firkovich EBP. I B 19a), copied in Cairo by Samuel ben Jacob and dated 1008/1009 AD, the oldest complete manuscript of the Hebrew Bible and the base text of the Biblia Hebraica editions. This chapter stands on folio 402r.

This entry meets the strict three-criteria standard of the Theosis Library:

  1. Manuscript scan: the specific folio side(s) carrying each section's verses, from the full-colour West Semitic Research Project photographs of the codex as redistributed on Internet Archive (item Leningrad_Codex_Color_Images, marked Creative Commons Public Domain Mark 1.0). Folio-to-verse ranges come from the tanach.us LC folio index, which was derived from the West Semitic Research Project's published index; each section links only to the page(s) whose recorded verse range contains its verses.
  2. Original text: the verbatim Hebrew of this manuscript in the Unicode/XML Leningrad Codex (UXLC 2.5 build 27.6, tanach.us), a transcription of Firkovich B 19a with vowels and cantillation, released without restriction on the biblical text.
  3. English translation: the King James Version (1611, public domain), retrieved verbatim from bolls.life (KJV text, Strong's numbers stripped).
translator_notes: פ and ס mark the open and closed paragraph breaks visible as gaps in the manuscript columns.

translation.original_text: <sup>1</sup>רוּחִ֣י חֻ֭בָּלָה יָמַ֥י נִזְעָ֗כוּ קְבָרִ֥ים לִֽי׃ <sup>2</sup>אִם־לֹ֣א הֲ֭תֻלִים עִמָּדִ֑י וּ֝בְהַמְּרוֹתָ֗ם תָּלַ֥ן עֵינִֽי׃ <sup>3</sup>שִֽׂימָה־נָּ֭א עַרְבֵ֣נִי עִמָּ֑ךְ מִֽי ה֝֗וּא לְיָדִ֥י יִתָּקֵֽעַ׃ <sup>4</sup>כִּֽי־לִ֭בָּם צָפַ֣נְתָּ מִשָּׂ֑כֶל עַל־כֵּ֝֗ן לֹ֣א תְרֹמֵֽם׃ <sup>5</sup>לְ֭חֵלֶק יַגִּ֣יד רֵעִ֑ים וְעֵינֵ֖י בָנָ֣יו תִּכְלֶֽנָה׃ <sup>6</sup>וְֽ֭הִצִּגַנִי לִמְשֹׁ֣ל עַמִּ֑ים וְתֹ֖פֶתּ לְפָנִ֣ים אֶֽהְיֶֽה׃ <sup>7</sup>וַתֵּ֣כַהּ מִכַּ֣עַשׂ עֵינִ֑י וִֽיצֻרַ֖י כַּצֵּ֣ל כֻּלָּֽם׃ <sup>8</sup>יָשֹׁ֣מּוּ יְשָׁרִ֣ים עַל־זֹ֑את וְ֝נָקִ֗י עַל־חָנֵ֥ף יִתְעֹרָֽר׃
translation.text: <sup>1</sup>My breath is corrupt, my days are extinct, the graves are ready for me. <sup>2</sup>Are there not mockers with me? and doth not mine eye continue in their provocation? <sup>3</sup>Lay down now, put me in a surety with thee; who is he that will strike hands with me? <sup>4</sup>For thou hast hid their heart from understanding: therefore shalt thou not exalt them. <sup>5</sup>He that speaketh flattery to his friends, even the eyes of his children shall fail. <sup>6</sup>He hath made me also a byword of the people; and aforetime I was as a tabret. <sup>7</sup>Mine eye also is dim by reason of sorrow, and all my members are as a shadow. <sup>8</sup>Upright men shall be astonied at this, and the innocent shall stir up himself against the hypocrite.

translation.original_text: <sup>9</sup>וְיֹאחֵ֣ז צַדִּ֣יק דַּרְכּ֑וֹ וּֽטֳהָר־יָ֝דַ֗יִם יֹסִ֥יף אֹֽמֶץ׃ <sup>10</sup>וְֽאוּלָ֗ם כֻּלָּ֣ם תָּ֭שֻׁבוּ וּבֹ֣אוּ נָ֑א וְלֹֽא־אֶמְצָ֖א בָכֶ֣ם חָכָֽם׃ <sup>11</sup>יָמַ֣י עָ֭בְרוּ זִמֹּתַ֣י נִתְּק֑וּ מ֖וֹרָשֵׁ֣י לְבָבִּֽי׃ <sup>12</sup>לַ֭יְלָה לְי֣וֹם יָשִׂ֑ימוּ א֝֗וֹר קָר֥וֹב מִפְּנֵי־חֹֽשֶׁךְ׃ <sup>13</sup>אִם־אֲ֭קַוֶּה שְׁא֣וֹל בֵּיתִ֑י בַּ֝חֹ֗שֶׁךְ רִפַּ֥דְתִּי יְצוּעָֽי׃ <sup>14</sup>לַשַּׁ֣חַת קָ֭רָאתִי אָ֣בִי אָ֑תָּה אִמִּ֥י וַ֝אֲחֹתִ֗י לָֽרִמָּֽה׃ <sup>15</sup>וְ֭אַיֵּה אֵפ֣וֹ תִקְוָתִ֑י וְ֝תִקְוָתִ֗י מִ֣י יְשׁוּרֶֽנָּה׃ <sup>16</sup>בַּדֵּ֣י שְׁאֹ֣ל תֵּרַ֑דְנָה אִם־יַ֖חַד עַל־עָפָ֣ר נָֽחַת׃ ס
translation.text: <sup>9</sup>The righteous also shall hold on his way, and he that hath clean hands shall be stronger and stronger. <sup>10</sup>But as for you all, do ye return, and come now: for I cannot find one wise man among you. <sup>11</sup>My days are past, my purposes are broken off, even the thoughts of my heart. <sup>12</sup>They change the night into day: the light is short because of darkness. <sup>13</sup>If I wait, the grave is mine house: I have made my bed in the darkness. <sup>14</sup>I have said to corruption, Thou art my father: to the worm, Thou art my mother, and my sister. <sup>15</sup>And where is now my hope? as for my hope, who shall see it? <sup>16</sup>They shall go down to the bars of the pit, when our rest together is in the dust.
